sections.title: Content — every setting
sections.summary: The headline, subtitle, and optional hero image — the words and lead visual that carry the screen. This guide documents every setting of the Content block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Content section
sections.summary: The Content section holds the words on the screen: your headline, supporting text, or the question you ask the visitor. This is the copy that does the persuading, so write it like ad copy with one clear value proposition or one focused question per screen, and edit it before you touch colors or layout. It's available on most screens with editable text; media-only and pure paywall screens use their own copy areas instead.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: HeroContent, ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, TextInput, WheelPicker, HeroList.

sections.title: How rounded the image is
sections.summary: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

sections.title: Size the image by screen
sections.summary: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

sections.title: Fixed image height
sections.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

sections.title: Space around the image
sections.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

sections.title: How the image fills its box
sections.summary: Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

sections.title: The hero image itself
sections.summary: Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

sections.title: Fixed image width
sections.summary: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

sections.title: The featured image up top
sections.summary: The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

sections.title: Where the image sits
sections.summary: On headline screens, this sets where the hero image sits relative to your title and subtitle — above the text, below it, or beside it. Lead with your strongest element: image-on-top when the visual is the hook, text-on-top when the headline does the selling. The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

sections.title: Space around the subtitle
sections.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

sections.title: Subtitle look and emphasis
sections.summary: Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. By default it inherits your theme (usually smaller and lighter than the title), which works for most funnels. Override only when a specific screen needs different emphasis.

sections.title: Write the subtitle text
sections.summary: Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

sections.title: The line under your title
sections.summary: The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

sections.title: Space around the title
sections.summary: Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

sections.title: Title look and emphasis
sections.summary: Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

sections.title: Write the headline text
sections.summary: This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

sections.title: Your main headline
sections.summary: The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

translations.en: Content — every setting

The headline, subtitle, and optional hero image — the words and lead visual that carry the screen. This guide documents every setting of the Content block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

en.name: The screen editor with the Content section highlighted.

translations.en: Open the Content section in the screen editor to configure its settings.
Title (headline)

en.name: Where the Title (headline) sits inside the open Content section.

translations.en: Inside the Content section, this is the Title (headline).
Your main headline

The title is the biggest, first thing a visitor reads, so it carries most of the weight on whether they keep going. Turn it on, then write one short benefit-led line, like an ad headline rather than a sentence. Type @ to drop in an earlier answer (for example @user_goal) so it feels personal, and style it under the gear icon below.

en.name: Where to find “Your main headline” in the editor.

translations.en: Write the headline text

This is where you type the actual headline; keep it short and benefit-driven. Type @ to pull in a visitor's earlier answer (such as @user_goal) for personalization, add a link inside the text with @link, or insert a countdown with @countdown to create urgency on offer screens. If your funnel runs in more than one language, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

en.name: Where to find “Write the headline text” in the editor.

translations.en: Title look and emphasis

Override how the headline looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional highlight behind the text. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent, so most funnels never need to touch this. Override only when one screen needs extra punch, like a bigger color headline on your hero.

en.name: Where to find “Title look and emphasis” in the editor.

translations.en: Space around the title

Adds empty space on each side of the title (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't cramped against the screen edges or the text below. Leave it at the theme default unless the title feels too tight or too far from the next element. Increase a side to give it room, or decrease to pull elements closer together.

en.name: Where to find “Space around the title” in the editor.

translations.en: Subtitle

en.name: Where the Subtitle sits inside the open Content section.

translations.en: Inside the Content section, this is the Subtitle.

nodes.label: Subtitle · The line under your title

translations.en: The line under your title

The subtitle is the supporting line beneath your title; use it to expand the promise, add proof, or hint at what happens next. Turn it on and keep it to one short sentence; it shows smaller and lighter than the title by default so the headline stays dominant. Like the title, you can personalize it with @ variables. Skip it on screens where the title already says everything.

en.name: Where to find “The line under your title” in the editor.

translations.en: Write the subtitle text

Type the supporting line that sits under your title here, one short sentence that reinforces the offer or tells the visitor what comes next. The same shortcuts work as in the title: type @ to insert an earlier answer, @link to add a clickable link, or @countdown for urgency. If your funnel is multilingual, text is saved per language, so switch language before editing each translation.

en.name: Where to find “Write the subtitle text” in the editor.

translations.en: Subtitle look and emphasis

Change how the subtitle looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and an optional background — styled separately from the title so you can tune each one. By default it inherits your theme (usually smaller and lighter than the title), which works for most funnels. Override only when a specific screen needs different emphasis.

en.name: Where to find “Subtitle look and emphasis” in the editor.

translations.en: Space around the subtitle

Adds empty space on each side of the subtitle, controlling the gap above it (to the title) and below it (to what follows). Leave it at the theme default unless the subtitle feels crowded. Increase the top value to separate it from the title, or reduce spacing to tighten the whole headline group.

en.name: Where to find “Space around the subtitle” in the editor.

translations.en: Hero image

en.name: Where the Hero image sits inside the open Content section.

translations.en: Inside the Content section, this is the Hero image.

nodes.label: Hero image · The featured image up top

translations.en: The featured image up top

The hero is the large featured image at the top of a headline or wheel-picker screen, the picture that sells the screen at a glance. Turn it on, then upload a file or paste an image URL. Pick a high-quality, on-message visual (product, result, or lifestyle shot); on a paid landing page it is often the first thing a visitor sees. Sizing and position are set just below.

en.name: Where to find “The featured image up top” in the editor.

nodes.label: Hero image · The hero image itself

translations.en: The hero image itself

Pick the actual hero image: upload a file from your computer or paste a direct image URL, then check the preview thumbnail. Use a high-resolution JPG or PNG so it stays crisp on large screens — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading. To change it later, just upload or paste a new source here.

en.name: Where to find “The hero image itself” in the editor.

nodes.label: Hero image · How the image fills its box

translations.en: How the image fills its box

Sets how your image fits its box: Aspect Fit shows the whole image with no cropping (you may see empty bars at the sides), Aspect Fill crops the edges so it fully covers the box, Scale to Fill stretches it (can look distorted, avoid for photos), and Tile repeats it as a pattern. Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

nodes.label: How the image fills its box

en.name: Where to find “How the image fills its box” in the editor.

translations.en: Fixed image width

Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

en.name: Where to find “Fixed image width” in the editor.

translations.en: Fixed image height

Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

en.name: Where to find “Fixed image height” in the editor.

nodes.label: Hero image · Size the image by screen

translations.en: Size the image by screen

Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

en.name: Where to find “Size the image by screen” in the editor.

nodes.label: Hero image · How rounded the image is

translations.en: How rounded the image is

Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

en.name: Where to find “How rounded the image is” in the editor.

nodes.label: Hero image · Space around the image

translations.en: Space around the image

Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

en.name: Where to find “Space around the image” in the editor.

translations.en: Image & text layout

nodes.label: Image & text layout · Where the image sits

translations.en: Where the image sits

On headline screens, this sets where the hero image sits relative to your title and subtitle — above the text, below it, or beside it. Lead with your strongest element: image-on-top when the visual is the hook, text-on-top when the headline does the selling. The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

en.name: Where to find “Where the image sits” in the editor.
